llm.summary: This skill is a disclosed AI KEY router and onboarding guide, with some local discovery, update-checking, and memory behavior users should understand before installing.

dimensions.detail: Local discovery is limited to AI KEY-family skill directories under common skill roots and the repository, though it can expose installed skill names/descriptions and real local paths to the agent.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: It includes shell scripts for local skill discovery and update notification. The update script fetches remote SKILL.md version metadata and prints an install/update command, but does not execute npx or modify installed skills.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill has broad natural-language triggers and tells the agent to route, read referenced guidance, and sometimes hand off to related AI KEY skills, but it repeatedly limits itself from doing downstream diagnosis or writing unless the user explicitly selects that path.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: The update script writes a daily timestamp under ~/.aikey, and the shared family guidance describes writing outputs and memory records in the configured vault. These behaviors are disclosed and purpose-aligned, but they are persistent local side effects.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

dimensions.detail: The artifacts coherently describe a routing entry point for AI KEY content and business skills, plus a guided onboarding mode and post-task navigation.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

llm.guidance: Install this if you want a Chinese-oriented AI KEY routing layer that can inspect your installed AI KEY skills, read configured vault/memory files, and keep lightweight local state. Be aware it may contact the public GitHub raw content endpoint once per day for version checks and may write persistent memory/output files as part of the AI KEY family workflow; review your config and vault paths before use.
llm.findings:
[TP4] unexpected: The automatic update check is ancillary to routing, but it is disclosed, rate-limited, fetches version metadata only, and does not execute remote code or perform updates.
[SDI-1] expected: The local skill discovery script supports the stated dynamic routing behavior and is read-only, but it does reveal local AI KEY skill inventory and paths.
[SDI-2] unexpected: Shell use for the update reminder is not essential to routing, but the inspected script is bounded to curl version checks, temporary files, and a timestamp; no destructive or remote execution behavior was found.
[TM1] expected: The flagged rm usage is confined to files inside a mktemp directory or failed curl output cleanup, not broad deletion.
[RP1] unexpected: The npx command is emitted as text for the user to run manually; the artifact does not execute it.
[LP3] expected: The manifest does not declare a narrow tool scope, but the runtime instructions name the two shell scripts and their behavior directly.
[SQP-1] expected: Broad trigger phrases are expected for a user-facing router and onboarding skill; the side effects are disclosed but users should know casual requests may activate it.
[SQP-3] expected: Most artifact text and examples are Chinese-focused, but the inspected instructions explicitly say to follow the user's language.
[AE1] unexpected: The referenced files were present locally and inspectable; no analysis-evasion behavior was supported by the artifact review.
